d2_fired.eliminating_machinery: A declared `sol-roundtrip` verifier returning PASS/FAIL/NO_VERIFIER_RAN for a named stage id.

d2_fired.cognition_required: Authoring the catalog entry and the two option patches for a subject the catalog did not already contain.
d2_fired.eliminating_machinery: A typed decision detector bound to the pipeline's own Findings objects, emitting question.key mechanically from (category, review_scope, action), so a novel subject is a catalog MISS that refuses rather than a judgement call.

d2_fired.cognition_required: Independence cannot be measured with one identity.
d2_fired.eliminating_machinery: A second principal (a distinct GitHub identity or a GitHub App installation token) plus an actor register the validator reads, so distinctness is MEASURED rather than asserted.

deviations.design_says: proof-b 3.1: the venue is one issue in a NEW control repository sbracewell64/fm-cleanroom-control.
deviations.deviation: The venue is ONE NEW issue on sbracewell64/firstmate-sol-control, titled with the required CLEANROOM-PROOF-B: prefix. Issues 2 and 19 are never touched and no retired-queue work item is referenced.
deviations.lost: The venue is not a clean-room-only repository; it coexists with unrelated retired-fleet issues.
deviations.preserved: One issue per correlation id; the comment universe of THIS issue is exactly ours and is completely observable, so the completeness predicate is unchanged.
deviations.reality: Browser Sol demonstrably watches the EXISTING private repository sbracewell64/firstmate-sol-control and rules there autonomously; a brand-new repository has no known Sol watcher, so a request posted only there might never be inspected. The executor's authority bound permits one issue and its comments, not a repository.

deviations.design_says: proof-b 3.1/4.4/4.5: schema, renderer, catalog and the SemVer reference live in the control repository and are referenced by blob-at-commit URL.
deviations.deviation: Those artifacts live in this attempt's pinned inputs/ and tools/. The exact schema-of-record bytes and the exact SemVer section 10 bytes are EMBEDDED in the issue body in fenced blocks, and reply_contract.schema_locator is an api_capture locator naming the posted issue body plus the schema sha256 - the treatment the design already prescribes for the mutable PR body (4.5).
deviations.lost: Locator immutability: an issue body is editable. Mitigated by capturing the posted body via the API immediately after posting, recording its sha256, and never editing it.
deviations.preserved: The ruler sees the exact bytes with no second fetch and can recompute vocabulary_digest.
deviations.reality: No repository may be created and the reachable control repository is not ours to commit to.

deviations.design_says: proof-b 4.5: read every evidence locator the way a third party would, unauthenticated.
deviations.deviation: B-S5 probes the SUBJECT evidence locators unauthenticated, which is the property that matters (the ruler must inspect the subject). Control-plane anonymous readability is a declared property of the chosen venue, recorded as a decision, not measured as a CNO.
deviations.lost: A ruler without repository access cannot read the request at all.
deviations.preserved: Every byte the ruling rests on is third-party resolvable and content-addressed.
deviations.reality: The reachable control repository is PRIVATE, so control-plane artifacts are not anonymously resolvable. The SUBJECT repository sbracewell64/fm-cleanroom-proof is public (archived, still publicly readable) and its locators ARE anonymously resolvable.

deviations.design_says: proof-b B-S2 prepares an OPEN, qualified candidate PR; BP6 accepts candidate_state in {STABLE_FOR_VALIDATION, VALIDATED_EXACT_HEAD}; L2 requires live PR state == "open".
deviations.deviation: The subject candidate is Proof A's LANDED candidate (branch fm-proof-a/semver-compare, published head 281e15b2, PR #2, state closed/merged, candidate_state ATTESTED). BP6's accepted set gains ATTESTED. L2 becomes: live PR state EQUALS the state recorded at compile time.
deviations.lost: The design's staging in which a ruling is consumed into a still-open candidate before it lands.
deviations.preserved: Both remain identity checks against machine state. BP6's anti-MUTATING intent holds STRICTLY MORE strongly: an archived repository's candidate cannot mutate at all. L2 still refuses a candidate that has moved out of the state the request was compiled against.
deviations.reality: sbracewell64/fm-cleanroom-proof is archived and read-only and its PR #2 is MERGED. The executor may not open a PR there and the brief prefers not unarchiving.

deviations.design_says: proof-b 10.1/11: an ADOPT_OPTION directive applies the option patch and lands it through Proof A's path.
deviations.deviation: B-S11 applies the ruled patch in a local scratch clone of the archived repository and runs the 10.2 identity check there. Nothing is pushed, no PR is opened, the repository is never unarchived. B-S13 is out of scope (see stages_out_of_scope).
deviations.lost: That the ruled change survives a qualification pipeline and lands under a fresh authorization.
deviations.preserved: F7 - the design's terminal claim - is exactly the applied-bytes identity check, and it is run.
deviations.reality: The subject repository is archived; the authority bound scopes application to a local scratch clone with the applied-bytes identity check and prefers not unarchiving.

deviations.design_says: proof-b 12 bolds 'Every FAIL and every CNO stops the proof at that stage', while the same table's independence-CNO row states its consequence as a GRADE ('proof grades CNO_AT_B-S9'), unlike its neighbouring rows which say 'consume nothing' and 'stop'.
deviations.deviation: PINNED RESOLUTION: V7's independence could-not-observe CAPS the terminal grade at CNO_AT_B-S9 and does not stop the proof. B-S10 through B-S12 still execute and are recorded, so F7's identity check is watched rather than skipped. The receipt carries V7's CNO verbatim in validation[] so no reader can mistake it for measured independence.
deviations.lost: Nothing measurable; the change is that MORE evidence is produced at the SAME grade. The residual risk - consuming a ruling whose independence is unmeasured - is bounded because the application is a local scratch clone that is never pushed.
deviations.preserved: The terminal grade is unchanged and cannot be inflated: CNO_AT_B-S9, explicitly not PROVED.
deviations.reality: The two readings differ and the ambiguity must be resolved before the answer is in view.

deviations.design_says: proof-b 15: ten falsifiers, each watched red first; several post malformed or duplicate rulings to the live venue.
deviations.deviation: Falsifiers run against the SAME ladder.py code path the live ruling passes through, using synthetic comment universes. Falsifier 6 also runs against the live fetch. Falsifiers 4 and 5's live halves (push a commit / change protection after the ruling) cannot run at all: the subject repository is archived and read-only, so their comparators are falsified with synthetic inputs and the live half is recorded in falsifier_limits.
deviations.lost: The live-forge half of falsifiers 3, 4, 5 and 7.
deviations.preserved: Every control that gates the live ruling is watched red for its own reason, with target and observed recorded and compared, before the first live observation.
deviations.reality: Posting six malformed, duplicate and mention-only comments into the live Sol-watched issue would pollute the venue the round trip depends on and could confuse the real ruler.

deviations.design_says: proof-b 4.3: expires_at := created_at + 72h; 7.3: the wait is code's job.
deviations.deviation: expires_at stays created_at + 72h - it is the REQUEST's validity window and a ruling arriving at hour three is still valid. The EXECUTOR's poll bound is 90 minutes (18 attempts, 300s apart). The two are different facts and are recorded apart.
deviations.lost: Nothing; the request outlives this executor's attention.
deviations.preserved: A non-answer is a recorded terminal state rather than an indefinite wait.

deviations.design_says: proof-b 12: no ruling before expires_at yields a receipt and the issue closes.
deviations.deviation: On executor-bound exhaustion a receipt comment is posted with outcome CNO_TRANSPORT and a note naming the 90-minute EXECUTOR bound (explicitly distinct from Sol answering INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE, and distinct from expiry), and the issue is LEFT OPEN.
deviations.lost: The design's close-on-terminal; closing here would discard a still-valid answer.
deviations.preserved: Every terminal state produces a receipt, so the request is never silently abandoned.
deviations.reality: The executor's 90-minute bound expires long before the request's 72h window.

deviations.design_says: proofs-shared-contracts 1.1: Proof B's schema $refs the shared $defs block of Proof A's.
deviations.deviation: tools/build_schema.py EXTRACTS the ten shared $defs programmatically from Proof A's schema file and embeds them, recording both digests. No definition is retyped.
deviations.lost: Automatic propagation if Proof A's schema were later edited; the recorded source digest makes that detectable rather than silent.
deviations.preserved: Exactly one AUTHORED definition of each shared type across both proofs.
deviations.reality: A cross-file $ref is unresolvable for a third party validating the schema that travels inline.

deviations_discovered_during_execution.decision: Captured as context in raw/check-runs-at-head.json and NOT carried as an evidence_ref. This decision rests on the module, its tests, the candidate diff and the normative anchor. A limitation the proof could enforce but chose not to is a DECISION NOT TO ENFORCE, recorded as such, not a could-not-observe.
deviations_discovered_during_execution.what: The design's 4.5 locator table lists the numeric check-run id at the candidate head as an evidence_ref. GitHub's check-runs API requires authentication even on a public repository, so it does not resolve for the unauthenticated third party B-S5 probes as.

falsifier_limits: No falsifier is posted to the live venue (DEV-B8), so the live-forge halves of falsifiers 3 and 7 are not run.

Falsifier 4's live half and falsifier 5's positive live half cannot be run at all: the subject repository is archived and read-only, so neither its head nor its protection can be moved. Their comparators are falsified with synthetic inputs; the end-to-end control is NOT watched red on the live forge.

instrument_defects_found_and_corrected.record_handling: Nothing appended was edited. B-S4 was re-run in full; both compiles are in the trace.
instrument_defects_found_and_corrected.what: candidate.base_sha was sourced from `git merge-base head origin/<default>`, but the default branch now CONTAINS the candidate, so it returned the head itself and the diff evidence locator would have resolved to an empty range.
instrument_defects_found_and_corrected.why_it_matters: The observation 'C:candidate.base_sha came from machine state' was TRUE and green while saying nothing about whether the field answered the right question - the wrong-subject failure. Two new gating predicates now check base != head and that the diff resolves non-empty.

instrument_defects_found_and_corrected.record_handling: Digests are now over raw bytes and locators are commit-pinned raw URLs; B-S4 re-run; all six locators then matched byte-for-byte.
instrument_defects_found_and_corrected.what: Blob evidence digests were taken over git output that had been .strip()ped, so they could never equal the sha256 of the bytes an anonymous reader receives.
instrument_defects_found_and_corrected.why_it_matters: The B-S5 readiness probe would have refused on an instrument artifact rather than on genuine inspectability - a fail-closed refusal for the wrong reason is still a wrong answer.

instrument_defects_found_and_corrected.record_handling: V7 gained an explicit identities_distinct input and all three values; F8b and F8c watch both branches and F0b re-confirms the green path. The original F8 observation is retained unedited.
instrument_defects_found_and_corrected.what: ladder.validation_ladder's V7 had no observed-bad branch, so falsifier 8 could only ever watch the could-not-observe path. Crediting F8 with 'the ruler-is-a-maker refusal was watched red' would have been the wrong-subject failure.

ruling.rationale: Adopt A. The module presents itself as SemVer 2.0.0 parsing and precedence comparison. SemVer 2.0.0 makes build metadata valid syntax while requiring it to be ignored only for precedence. A resolves the current mismatch without silently discarding caller data because parse preserves the metadata and compare ignores it only on the precedence axis. B would deliberately keep valid SemVer inputs uncomparable and force callers to duplicate suffix-stripping logic outside the parser. The selected change is bounded to the pure module/tests, has no new dependency or reserved-path effect, and is explicitly single-commit reversible. This ruling selects the engineering option only; it does not waive exact-bytes application checks, tests, provenance, maker/checker separation, or any protected-effect gate.
